research.topic: The Arctic tern (Sterna paradisaea) makes the longest known animal migration. Geolocator tracking of birds from Greenland and Iceland (Egevang et al., PNAS 2010) recorded an average round trip of about 70,900 km a year (up to 81,600 km), following an S-shaped route down the Atlantic to the Weddell Sea off Antarctica and back. Over a lifetime of about 30 years that adds up to roughly 2.4 million km, about three return trips to the Moon (Audubon; Britannica). It breeds in the Arctic and sub-Arctic summer and winters at the Antarctic ice edge, so it experiences two summers a year and more daylight than any other animal (Britannica; Audubon). It weighs about 90–120 g (Cornell All About Birds). Humpback whales migrate about 8,000 km each way (up to ~8,300 km one way recorded, NOAA; Britannica); monarch butterflies travel up to about 4,800 km to Mexico (US Fish & Wildlife Service).

myths.myth: The longest migration must belong to a whale — the humpback crosses whole oceans.
myths.reality: The humpback covers about 8,000 km each way; the Arctic tern's yearly round trip is around 70,000 km, pole to pole and back.
